headline: How common dust makes clouds freeze
standfirst: Scientists have found why tiny mineral particles act as seeds for ice crystals in the sky.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers discovered how the mineral microcline triggers ice formation in clouds.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Pure water usually stays liquid until it hits -38°C. Dust particles help it freeze sooner.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Understanding these ice nucleators helps us track how clouds form and change our weather.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future studies will explore how other mineral dust types affect cloud behavior.

caption:
Scientists at Bielefeld University have identified how the mineral microcline helps clouds form ice crystals.

Pure water is stubborn and doesn't freeze until it reaches extreme cold. Tiny particles of dust act as a shortcut, giving ice a surface to grow on at warmer temperatures. This research helps us understand the complex physics happening high above our heads.
